name: gaia-no-permanent-hang
phase: gaia hardening -- fixed the actual root cause of complete unresponsiveness
pass_condition: GET /api/gaia always eventually responds (never hangs indefinitely). A live drill: kill the running gaia_server, restart, issue 3 sequential requests then 5 CONCURRENT requests -- every request returns 200 with a full multi-seat envelope within a bounded time (observed: sequential 3-4.4s each; 5 concurrent requests resolve together in ~3.1s total via single-flight coalescing).
falsifies_condition: Any request to /api/gaia or a seat route never returns (client times out at 60s+); OR the server accumulates CLOSE_WAIT sockets that never get a response; OR a restarted server repeats the same permanent hang.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (found live 2026-07-14): viewer/infra.cjs's cached() helper stored a pending promise and returned it unconditionally on every call while pending, with NO ceiling on how long "pending" could last. A single transient hang inside one cached source (SSH child process, DNS query) poisoned that cache entry PERMANENTLY -- every subsequent request for the life of the process awaited the same never-resolving promise. Live-confirmed: the running gaia_server (pid 3096, started 16:56) had accumulated 30+ CLOSE_WAIT sockets that never got a response over roughly 3.5 hours, while an isolated fresh-process test showed every individual collector completing cleanly in ~9.5s total -- proving the bug was permanently-stuck cache state, not slow work. FIX (four layers, all in this session): (1) infra.cjs cached() now races fn() against a FIXED 10s hang-ceiling (decoupled from cache-freshness TTL, which was originally reused as the ceiling and let slow-refreshing sources hang up to 30s before self-healing) and DELETES the cache entry on timeout/rejection so the next poll gets a fresh attempt instead of being wedged forever; (2) gaia.cjs's gaia() was rewritten from a fully sequential await-chain (one hung collector blocked every collector after it AND every future request) to two parallel Promise.all phases (source collectors, then introspective collectors), each collector individually raced against a 20s per-collector ceiling that degrades to "no signals this seat" on timeout rather than propagating the hang; (3) gaia_server.cjs adds a 45s transport-level ceiling around the whole gaia() call plus single-flight request coalescing (concurrent callers share one in-flight computation instead of each paying the full cost independently -- closes the compounding-latency case measured live once the UNI-HUD native service's 12s poll of /api/gaia/drift was found overlapping with manual test requests); (4) three internally-sequential per-item loops were parallelized (infra.cjs dnsDrift() 17-name DNS loop, collectors.cjs studioProbeSignals() N-service loop, colonyProbeSignals() 4-probe loop) since none had a data dependency between iterations. Live-verified end to end: killed the poisoned process, restarted, 3 sequential GET /api/gaia calls returned 200 in 3.2s/2.9s/4.4s, 5 CONCURRENT GET /api/gaia calls all returned 200 within one shared ~3.1s window (single-flight proof), full envelope both times (129 signals across all 9 seats, no seat dropped). node viewer/gaia/verify_gaia.cjs re-run post-fix: 11 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP, no regression.
